content:
This is your sketch, not your statement — but even a sketch this rough tells me something worth acting on.

Your fixed base sits at ≈£1,170/mo against a £3,100 take-home, leaving ≈£1,930 free. Eating out accounts for ≈£60 of that. Your could-save reach is ≈£100. That leaves ≈£1,770 a month unaccounted for — drifting somewhere, direction unknown. The pot is a direction right now, not a dated target, and that's fine. The question is just whether money starts moving toward it.

The move: set up a standing transfer of ≈£300/mo on payday. It's sized at roughly half the drift, so it won't bite. At that pace the pot lands in ≈3 months. Left as it is, closer to ≈10.

You called the ≈£1,770 drift unsure — and that's the honest call. A real month says whether it's one big category you forgot to name, or whether it genuinely is scattered spending with no pattern. That answer changes everything about what to do next.

Checking a real month does two things: it swaps every ≈ for an actual number so you can see estimate versus reality side by side, and it fills in the habits half of the picture — timing, what's recurring, what spikes — which estimates can't see at all. That's where the security picture gets real.

Right now, I know you about 56%. Checking a real month is what takes that past 70%.

[CTA:start_statement_check]Check my numbers[/CTA]

— C.
